title: Finite net from a maximal disjoint family of closed balls (packing count)
statement: Let X be a metric space whose sigma-algebra contains all open sets (so closed balls are measurable), and let mu be a measure on X. Let S, E be subsets of X and r, a, b real numbers with r > 0, a > 0, b >= 0 and mu(E) <= b. Assume that for every y in S the closed ball B_r(y) = {x : dist(x,y) <= r} is contained in E and mu(B_r(y)) >= a. Then there is a finite set F contained in S with (#F) * a <= b such that every y in S satisfies dist(y, z) <= 2r for some z in F.
lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (S E : Set X) (r a b : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 < a → 0 ≤ b → μ E ≤ ENNReal.ofReal b → (∀ y ∈ S, closedBall y r ⊆ E ∧ ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ μ (closedBall y r)) → ∃ F : Finset X, (↑F : Set X) ⊆ S ∧ (F.card : ℝ) * a ≤ b ∧ ∀ y ∈ S, ∃ z ∈ F, dist y z ≤ 2 * r
